items.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.description: The US has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, a critically-needed munition for defence against escalating Russian aerial attacks, after Kyiv said deliveries had been delayed in recent months. The US State Department said the advanced PAC-3 interceptor missiles would cost $2.1bn (£1.6bn) and would be “funded entirely” by Kyiv’s allies in Europe and Canada. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has repeatedly urged the US to speed up deliveries of its Patriots – the only effective weapon in downing Russia’s deadly ballistic missiles. The latest move comes just days after a row between Zelensky and Donald Trump, with the US president saying it was time for Ukraine to get a new leader to try to end the war with Russia. In Friday’s statement, the State Department said “this proposed sale will support the foreign policy and national security objectives of the United States by improving the security of a partner country that is a force for political and economic stability in Europe”. It said “Ukraine will pay for this purchase with donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan”. The statement said the “principal contractor” would be American company Lockheed Martin, adding that “no US funds are involved in this sale”. Zelensky said earlier this week that his country had been waiting almost a month for the US to sign off on critical missile supplies. And in a Telegram post late on Friday, the Ukrainian president reported that earlier in the day Russian ballistic missiles had struck two of the country’s regions. “They continue to carry out terrorist strikes against our cities,” he said. Zelensky has recently admitted that Ukraine was running critically low on Patriots, as Russia was intensifying its attacks on key energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Kyiv desperately needs the interceptors but there is a global shortage of the munitions due to their use by the US in its war against Iran. It is not clear what the production schedule will be for the Patriots – but it is understood the order is for new builds rather than existing missiles, meaning there is unlikely to be any kind of rapid delivery to Ukraine. Patriots also have lengthy production times, with only 600 missiles produced per year according to the US Department of Defence.

items.title: Tunisiens et Canadiens réunis à Gammarth pour penser l’éducation de demain
items.description: L'Ambassadeur canadien Alexandre Bilodeau a tenu à être présent à l'ouverture de la 5e édition du Forum citoyen international de l'éducation et de la recherche interdisciplinaire (FCIERI 2026). Ce forum, porté par des binationaux tuniso-canadiens, est consacré cette année à la transition numérique et durable. L'Ambassadeur a salué à cette occasion le rôle de la diaspora tunisienne au Canada, un pont vivant entre nos deux pays : ce forum en est la preuve ! Jusqu'au 1er novembre, 120 intervenants canadiens y partagent la tribune avec leurs collègues tunisiens, sur des sujets aussi pertinents que l'intelligence artificielle, la réforme de l'Éducation et le développement durable. Un immense merci aux équipes du Forum tunisien pour l'éducation (FTE) et de l'association ARDHI, grâce à qui ce rendez-vous né en 2017 ne cesse de grandir. Vivement les projets communs qui en sortiront ! items.title: A Very Bad 24 Hours for Crypto
items.description: This is an edition of Over/Under, a newsletter on the latest in prediction markets, gambling, and the evolution of everyday risk. Sign up here. Last night, hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange. The whole thing reportedly took about 20 minutes. It was the biggest theft in the history of the sector, and also probably the biggest financial heist of all time, topping the $1.5 billion ByBit hack of 2025 and Sadam Hussein’s $1 billion robbery of the Central Bank of Iraq in 2003. Binance says that about half of the stolen funds have been “frozen”—meaning that they’re effectively banned from being used in future transactions. North Korean hackers are thought to have been responsible. In the hours before the attack, though, a smaller heist was roiling a different corner of digital finance: Yesterday afternoon, at least $2.6 million was reportedly drained from Polymarket accounts. This, too, was a crypto theft. Polymarket’s international platform, which until last month hosted the majority of the company’s trading volume, runs on blockchain technology. But the attacks had different origins, and there’s no evidence that the two are connected. Binance is saying that its hack may have involved a compromised laptop, as well as “additional points of breach”; thieves took money that was stored on the exchange. On Polymarket, hackers exploited a flaw in a third-party provider, allowing them to access users’ accounts. It was the firm’s second security lapse since June. Both platforms say they plan to cover the losses in full. But in crypto, getting your money back isn’t a guarantee. Despite the technical differences and massive disparity in scale, yesterday’s hacks are a reminder that crypto-backed platforms of all kinds can still come with fundamental risks. Unlike Kalshi, which has a single U.S. exchange for its domestic and international customers, Polymarket’s operations are split down the middle: Polymarket.com and Polymarket.us are two separate exchanges. When you make a bet on the U.S. site, your trade is settled in dollars. On the international site, everything is settled in crypto. The distinction matters . Both traditional financial firms and blockchain-backed systems face immense cybersecurity challenges —and the crypto industry has done a lot of growing up since 2022—but with crypto, customers typically have less recourse when things go wrong. Although deposits at U.S. banks are technically IOUs, they tend to be really good IOUs. If you ask for your money, you can be pretty confident that it will be there. If the bank fails, you’re guaranteed to get some of it back, thanks to the miracle of FDIC insurance. Polymarket, like Binance, isn’t a bank, and its international platform isn’t overseen by the American regulatory system. (Both companies’ independent U.S. platforms, which are subject to onshore regulations, were entirely unaffected by these attacks.) Users may get their money back this time, as the firms have promised, but that’s not always the case—not all companies have the funds to repay their customers. They’re not necessarily obligated to, either. Polymarket’s ties to crypto go back to its founding, in 2020, a moment when the industry was seen as a kind of Wild West. Early on, users could make bets on the site only if they were willing to ditch old-school money for digital tokens. Polymarket didn’t even have a domestic, non-crypto platform until late last year—and until very recently , it was seeing less volume than the international site. (The demographics for crypto and prediction markets still have some overlap too.) This isn’t the end for Polymarket, and it’s certainly not the end for crypto, which has lately proved itself to be incredibly resilient. (Bitcoin is down a few thousand dollars since last night, but it hasn’t tanked nearly as much as you might expect after a disruption of this scale.) Still, the timing is unfortunate for the company. As I wrote on Wednesday, next week’s election coverage will put prediction markets in front of even more people. Users who have lost confidence in the company may end up switching over to Polymarket’s main competitor, Kalshi; users who aren’t familiar with prediction markets will have yet another reason to avoid them. Americans are already broadly skeptical of these firms’ push into politics. Polymarket’s link to crypto—and to the chaos of the past 24 hours—could further entrench that distrust. Possible Futures In every edition, I’ll share my thoughts on a few news stories I’m watching. On Wednesday, Utah’s attorney general filed 14 criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders, alleging that the company has been running a gambling platform against state rules. Both DraftKings and FanDuel have pulled some of their markets from the state, and Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig has pushed back, writing that Utah’s move sets a “dangerous precedent.” The agency is also suing the state (and many others ), alleging that prediction markets can be regulated only on the federal level.

items.title: Sahara : le Maroc tourne la page de la MINURSO et appelle au retrait du dossier de l’agenda onusien
items.description: Dans un communiqué publié vendredi 30 octobre, le Cabinet royal présente la non-reconduction du mandat de la MINURSO comme un tournant dans le dossier du Sahara marocain. Rabat évoque non seulement la fin de 35 années de présence de la mission onusienne dans les provinces du Sud, mais également le retrait de la question de l'ordre du jour du Conseil de sécurité, la fin de ses réunions périodiques et la suspension du processus politique onusien. Le Maroc entend désormais poursuivre sa dynamique diplomatique en faveur du plan d'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine. Le communiqué du Cabinet royal marque une prise de position majeure sur la nouvelle étape que le Maroc entend donner au dossier du Sahara. À la suite de la non-reconduction du mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l'organisation d'un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO), Rabat annonce une évolution qui dépasse la seule question de la présence de cette mission sur le terrain et touche directement aux modalités du suivi du dossier au sein des Nations unies. Le Cabinet royal qualifie cette évolution de « pas significatif vers la clôture définitive du dossier du Sahara marocain aux Nations unies ». Il l'inscrit dans le contexte de la célébration de la Fête de l'Unité, décrétée par le Roi Mohammed VI, et y voit une rupture avec une approche fondée jusque-là sur la gestion du différend, au profit d'une transformation profonde de ses paramètres. Le message central du communiqué est ainsi celui d'un changement de cycle : après 35 années de présence de la MINURSO et de suivi régulier du dossier par les instances onusiennes, le Maroc considère que les conditions d'une nouvelle phase sont désormais réunies. Vers le retrait du dossier de l'ordre du jour du Conseil de sécurité L'un des passages les plus importants du communiqué concerne explicitement l'avenir du dossier au sein des Nations unies. Le texte estime que la non-reconduction du mandat de la MINURSO devrait marquer la fin de la saisine du Conseil de sécurité et le retrait de la question du Sahara de son ordre du jour. Cette évolution aurait ainsi des conséquences directes sur le mécanisme de suivi du dossier. Les réunions statutaires périodiques du Conseil de sécurité consacrées au Sahara, les rapports du Secrétaire général des Nations unies ainsi que les briefings de son Envoyé personnel n'auraient dès lors plus lieu d'être. Le Cabinet royal considère également que le processus politique onusien se trouve suspendu. Il attribue cette situation aux blocages et aux tergiversations des autres parties, qui contribuent ainsi à prolonger le statu quo. Le texte annonce par ailleurs que des démarches similaires seront prochainement engagées au sein des autres organes des Nations unies. La fin de 35 années de présence de la MINURSO Le communiqué revient également sur la présence de la MINURSO dans les provinces du Sud depuis 35 ans, notant que la non-reconduction de son mandat signifie que la présence de la mission devrait cesser dans les prochains jours, notamment à travers le retrait de son personnel, de ses véhicules, de ses équipements et de ses symboles. Pour le Maroc, cette page est désormais tournée, en ce sens que la mission, héritée d'un contexte aujourd'hui dépassé, a longtemps constitué un instrument d'internationalisation du différend régional relatif au recouvrement par le Maroc de ses provinces sahariennes. Le plan d'autonomie au centre de la nouvelle dynamique Le Cabinet royal insiste sur la poursuite de la dynamique internationale engagée par le Roi Mohammed VI en faveur de la proposition marocaine d'autonomie. Le communiqué précise que cette orientation se poursuivra aux niveaux bilatéral et régional. Pour mesurer l'ampleur de cette dynamique, le texte avance que plus des deux tiers des États membres des Nations unies, y compris des membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité et des puissances influentes, soutiennent clairement l'autonomie sous souveraineté marocaine comme seul cadre de solution au différend régional. Le Cabinet royal a également tenu à préciser que cette évolution ne modifie pas l'attachement du Maroc au cessez-le-feu. Le Royaume affirme maintenir cet engagement dans le strict respect de son intégrité territoriale, de sa sécurité nationale et de la quiétude de ses citoyens. The post Sahara : le Maroc tourne la page de la MINURSO et appelle au retrait du dossier de l’agenda onusien appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tounes Clean up | Opération de nettoyage au centre historique du Kef
items.description: Une importante action de nettoyage et de sensibilisation environnementale a été menée dans le centre historique du Kef par l'association Tounes Clean Up. La mobilisation des participants et des bénévoles a permis de retirer près d'une tonne de détritus des ruelles et sites emblématiques de la ville. Au terme de cette journée, le bilan fait état de 828 kilogrammes de déchets collectés, indique Tounes Clean Up en précisant que la récolte comprend 500 kilogrammes de verre, 288 kilogrammes de déchets non recyclables ainsi que 40 kilogrammes de matières valorisables. La même source a par ailleurs remercié son partenaire Orange pour son soutien, à la municipalité du Kef et l'association Tunisie Recyclage, chargée de l'acheminement et de la revalorisation des matériaux récupérés ainsi qu'à tous les bénévoles et partenaires locaux pour leur engagement. Y. N. L’article Tounes Clean up | Opération de nettoyage au centre historique du Kef est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Ghana and Burkina Faso seek stronger trade and industrial cooperation at SIAO 2026
items.description: Ghana has reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening trade and investment relations with Burkina Faso through a proposed bilateral trade agreement aimed at promoting industrial cooperation, cross-border trade and value addition. The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, announced this during the opening ceremony of the 18th International Arts and Crafts Fair of Ouagadougou (SIAO 2026) on Friday, October 30. Delivering the Guest of Honour address, she highlighted opportunities for the two countries to collaborate in handicrafts, agro-processing, shea, cotton, leather and agricultural value chains. Ghana, which is participating as Guest of Honour alongside Mali and Niger, is showcasing products from all 16 regions at the fair. The exhibition features a range of Ghanaian products, including Kente, Adinkra, fugu, Bolgatanga baskets, beads, pottery, leather goods and contemporary fashion. Madam Ofosu-Adjare disclosed that formal trade between Ghana and Burkina Faso exceeded US$1 billion last year. She stressed the need to strengthen border management, harmonise product standards and facilitate the movement of goods between the two countries to further expand trade. The proposed bilateral agreement is expected to provide a framework for advancing cooperation and creating opportunities for businesses in both countries.

items.title: Savannah College of Education teachers decry 19 months without payroll migration
items.description: About one hundred and seventy striking workers of two local associations at the Savannah College of Education, namely, the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana [CETAG] and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana (CENTSAG), say the unresolved issues surrounding staff remuneration, recruitment and migration of members to the government payroll are a threat to their welfare and the smooth administration of the college. “Our concern is not to undermine government efforts or disregard the progress made since the college became a public institution. Rather, we seek to draw attention to the unresolved issues surrounding staff remuneration, recruitment and migration onto the government payroll, which continue to threaten staff and the smooth administration of the college,” they indicated. In a joint press conference in Daboya in the Savannah Region, members of the associations said the transition of the college into the public system can not be deemed complete while staff continue to work without government-paid salaries and a clear roadmap for their migration. Established in 2022, the Savannah College of Education was, among other things, to contribute to teacher preparation and help address the shortage of professional teachers in the region and beyond. But in 2024, the college came under mounting pressure from the student body regarding its private status. In response, the government subsequently absorbed the college in March, 2025 after an assessment by the Ghana Tertiary Education Council (G-TEC) in the public colleges of education. Fast forward, students were put on an allowance, no fee stress, and a pick-up vehicle to the college. But the teachers said they have yet to realise the benefits of the public status of the college. According to the press statement signed by the leadership of the two associations, Abdalla Abdul-Rahim for CENTSAG and Franklin Aguuri of CETAG said they recognised the importance and the need to integrate it into the public teacher education system and are yet to reap its full benefits. “The absorption raised legitimate expectations that the college would gradually enjoy the same institutional support, administration arrangements, and staff remuneration framework as other public colleges of education.” “Unfortunately, while some aspects of the transition have progressed, the situation regarding staff remuneration and migration remains unresolved.” While acknowledging government financial obligations to students, the workers expressed concern over what they described as government inconsistencies in the implementation of the transition. “Particularly the apparent disparity between the support extended to students and infrastructure and the unresolved welfare of staff.” “Our greatest concern, however, is the fact that no staff member of the Savannah College of Education has received salary from the Government since the college’s absorption in March, 2025. “Our staff is not asking for special treatment but for the fair and timely remuneration that should accompany our service in a public institution,” they indicated. One other major grievance that the teachers have attributed as an obstacle driving their plights is the delay in resolving the staff migration challenge in establishing the College’s Management Unit. “The creation of the Management Unit is critical to providing the administrative framework required for the effective management of the college and the processing of staff migration. Despite efforts by the leadership of the college and other stakeholders to address the situation, the process has not progressed as expected.” The striking, however, lamented that the continued uncertainty has created considerable anxiety among staff, particularly because the Management Unit is closely connected to the prospects of resolving their remuneration and migration, not forgetting the lack of a governing council for the college.

items.title: Changfans on River Tano have reduced thanks to NAIMOS – NAIMOS Spokesperson
items.description: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) says the number of changfan machines operating on the River Tano has reduced significantly following sustained enforcement under its Operation Water Shield campaign against illegal mining. In a Facebook post on Friday, October 30, 2026, the NAIMOS spokesperson, Paa Kwesi Schandorf, said a team of 15 journalists had accompanied officials to the river earlier in the day to assess the impact of the operation. He said the visit gave the journalists an opportunity to observe and independently assess the progress of the anti-galamsey campaign along the river and its surrounding areas. “The most crucial development to report is that changfans on River Tano HAVE GREATLY REDUCED,” Mr Schandorf wrote, crediting the sustained operations led by the Director of Operations at NAIMOS, Colonel K. S. Appiah. Sustained operations Mr Schandorf said NAIMOS would maintain surveillance on the Tano and other critical water sources as the government pursued efforts to restore polluted water bodies to their natural state. He cautioned, however, that the reduction in mining equipment did not mean the river had already been restored to its original condition. “The destruction of hundreds of changfans on the Tano River doesn’t immediately make it pure, but it’s a crucial starting point,” he said. He added that further measures would be taken under the leadership of the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, to protect and restore affected water bodies. Operation Water Shield Operation Water Shield is a sustained, intelligence-led enforcement campaign launched by NAIMOS in September 2026 to protect major rivers, watersheds and other critical water resources from illegal mining. The campaign seeks to move beyond isolated raids by targeting illegal mining activities along river systems, dismantling the machinery used in the operations and preventing miners from returning to areas cleared by security teams. Its priority water bodies include the Birim, Ankobra, Tano, Bia, Pra and Offin rivers, as well as affected sections of the Black and White Volta systems. The operation has already seen enforcement action along the Tano River. On October 19, for example, NAIMOS destroyed 92 changfan machines and arrested three suspected illegal miners during an operation at Asemkrom in the Aowin Municipality of the Western North Region. The operation targeted mining platforms and equipment operating directly on the river near the Jema-Asekrom Forest Reserve. NAIMOS has said the broader strategy includes sustained patrols and surveillance to prevent illegal miners from reoccupying cleared areas, alongside action against the networks and equipment suppliers that facilitate illegal mining. Focus on water-body recovery The latest assessment comes amid continuing concerns over the environmental damage caused by galamsey, including pollution of rivers and the degradation of surrounding land. Mr Schandorf said the reduction in changfans was an important step but indicated that further work would be needed to secure the river and support its recovery. He said NAIMOS would continue its surveillance and enforcement efforts in line with President John Dramani Mahama’s vision of restoring water bodies to their natural condition. The challenge now is to sustain the gains, prevent illegal mining from returning and establish measurable improvements in the condition of the River Tano.

items.title: PLF 2027 : Barik pointe les disparités fiscales et le déficit d'infrastructures dans les montagnes
items.description: Le débat autour du projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 a été l'occasion, vendredi, de mettre en lumière les difficultés quotidiennes des populations des régions montagneuses. Devant la Commission des finances et du développement économique à la Chambre des représentants, Abdelaziz Oussama Barik, député du Parti de l'unité et de la démocratie (PUD), a dénoncé les insuffisances des politiques publiques en matière de justice territoriale, d'adaptation climatique et d'accès aux services essentiels. Pour l'élu, la question du pouvoir d'achat ne peut se limiter à l'évolution des prix des produits alimentaires, notamment les oignons et les tomates. Dans les territoires montagneux, la hausse du coût du bois de chauffage constitue également une préoccupation majeure. Le prix du quintal atteint désormais 200 dirhams, alors que la saison hivernale n'a pas encore commencé. Une situation susceptible de s'aggraver avec la baisse des températures, a-t-il averti. Le parlementaire a appelé à intégrer ces contraintes dans les politiques publiques, à l'instar des mesures prises pour limiter la spéculation sur les produits alimentaires et en faciliter l'accès aux consommateurs. Il s'est également interrogé sur l'absence de dimension climatique dans le programme gouvernemental, estimant que les territoires soumis à des conditions naturelles difficiles nécessitent des dispositifs spécifiques. Au-delà de la question climatique, Oussama Barik a pointé les disparités territoriales dans la répartition des investissements et l'accès aux infrastructures. Il a notamment reproché au projet de loi de finances de privilégier les aspects fiscaux sans apporter de réponses suffisantes à la question de l'équité entre les régions. Selon lui, l'application des mêmes obligations fiscales à des citoyens qui ne bénéficient pas du même niveau d'équipement et de services publics pose un problème de justice. Dans certaines zones, l'état dégradé des routes, l'absence d'autoroutes et le déficit d'infrastructures obligent les habitants à supporter des dépenses supplémentaires, notamment pour réparer leurs véhicules endommagés par les nids-de-poule et les routes détériorées. Le député a plaidé pour des mesures tenant compte de ces contraintes et conformes aux objectifs de la régionalisation avancée. L'élu a également soulevé les difficultés rencontrées par les jeunes ayant opté pour le statut d'auto-entrepreneur, encouragés par les orientations gouvernementales en faveur de l'initiative individuelle. Certains se retrouvent aujourd'hui redevables d'obligations fiscales alors qu'ils n'ont jamais exercé d'activité génératrice de revenus. Cette situation peut même les empêcher d'accéder à certains services administratifs et sociaux, notamment l'inscription à la Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale (CNSS) et à la couverture médicale, en raison des sommes qu'ils doivent régler. Oussama Barik a ainsi demandé un réexamen de leur situation et des dettes accumulées dans le cadre de ce dispositif, afin de tenir compte de l'absence de revenus effectifs chez une partie des jeunes concernés. Les insuffisances de l'offre sanitaire ont constitué un autre volet de son intervention. Déplorant le manque d'infrastructures médicales dans les territoires concernés, le député a résumé la situation par une formule sans détour : « Nous n'avons pas d'hôpitaux, nous avons des stations d'ambulances ». Il faisait ainsi référence à des centres de santé qui, faute de moyens et de structures adaptées, se limiteraient à orienter les patients vers d'autres établissements, sans leur fournir les soins nécessaires sur place. Certains malades doivent notamment financer leur déplacement jusqu'à Errachidia pour accéder à des soins. Une charge supplémentaire que le parlementaire juge difficilement justifiable dans des territoires où les structures hospitalières de proximité font défaut. Il a appelé à renforcer l'offre de soins et à rapprocher les infrastructures sanitaires des populations. La valorisation des productions locales a également été au cœur de son intervention. Prenant l'exemple de la filière des pommes, le député de la circonscription de Midelt a relevé un écart important entre les prix pratiqués dans les zones de production et ceux observés dans les grandes villes. Selon les chiffres qu'il a avancés, le kilogramme de pommes est vendu autour de 5 dirhams dans certaines régions productrices, contre 15 à 20 dirhams à Rabat et Casablanca. Pour l'élu, cette différence témoigne des difficultés persistantes de commercialisation et des limites des circuits de distribution. Il a appelé à mieux intégrer les producteurs locaux dans les chaînes de valeur afin qu'ils puissent tirer davantage profit de leurs récoltes, au lieu de voir se creuser l'écart entre les prix à la production et ceux payés par les consommateurs. Enfin, le député a dénoncé des irrégularités présumées dans la réalisation de certains projets routiers. Il a notamment cité le cas d'une route de huit kilomètres, pour laquelle une enveloppe de 3,5 milliards de centimes, soit 35 millions de dirhams, aurait été mobilisée. Un montant dont l'importance ne se refléterait pas, selon lui, dans la qualité des travaux exécutés. Oussama Barik a rapporté les plaintes des habitants concernant les conditions de réalisation du chantier, affirmant que l'entrepreneur accueillerait leurs contestations « avec mépris ». Il a appelé à renforcer les contrôles et à faire prévaloir le principe de reddition des comptes pour garantir la conformité des travaux aux normes requises et prévenir le gaspillage ainsi que la mauvaise gestion des deniers publics. The post PLF 2027 : Barik pointe les disparités fiscales et le déficit d'infrastructures dans les montagnes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Yagbonwura appeals to Mahama to intervene in Savannah College of Education staff strike
items.description: The Overlord of Gonjaland and Life Patron of the Savannah College of Education, Yagbonwura Bii-Kunuto Jewu Soale I, has appealed to President John Dramani Mahama to intervene in the ongoing strike by teaching and non-teaching staff of the institution. According to him, the industrial action, which has entered its fifth day, is a major concern for the college and the Savannah Region, and requires urgent presidential intervention to get the workers back to work. “I know and believe that my Son, the President, says yes, the challenges will be solved. So, what we need to hear from him now is to talk to his officers to address the workers’ grievances, if not all, but the major ones.” The Overlord appealed in an interview with JoyNews through the Secretary to the Wasipe Traditional Council, Jantonwura Peter Awusi Yakubu, in Daboya. The Overlord is particularly concerned about the impact of the strike on students, with kitchen staff also joining the industrial action. He says the situation has disrupted food services at the college, leaving students without meals prepared on campus. “I heard the cooks are also on strike, and it becomes a double problem because the chiefs I sent to the college came back and told me that the school doesn’t even have food to feed the students. This is very serious.” About 170 teaching and non-teaching staff, drawn from the Colleges of Education Teachers Association of Ghana and the Colleges of Education Non-Teaching Staff Association of Ghana, are participating in the strike. The workers are demanding their migration onto the public payroll system, saying they have not received payment for their services since the college was absorbed by the government in March 2025. They are also demanding the establishment of the college Management Unit to work on their migration to the public payroll. They also claim the situation has contributed to the departure of 17 teachers to other colleges of education. A visit by JoyNews to the college’s kitchen revealed that both the kitchen and pantry had been locked, leaving students to make alternative arrangements for their meals outside the campus. The strike has heightened tension on campus and raised concerns about the welfare of students and the need for an urgent resolution to the dispute.

items.title: Debibi United President fires back at GoldStars coach over cassava pitch comment
items.description: Debibi United Chief Executive Officer, Alexander Ababio, has hit back at the coach of Bibiani GoldStars Petros Koukouras over his comments about the club’s playing pitch, describing the remarks as reckless and unreasonable. After Gold Stars suffered a 1-0 defeat to Debibi United in the 2026/27 Ghana Premier League Matchday 7, the Greek coach expressed his displeasure over the state of the Debibi Presby Park, describing the playing surface as more suitable for cassava farming than football. Speaking to Nhyira FM, Mr Ababio expressed his displeasure with Perto’s statement, questioning the reasoning behind the comparison involving cassava cultivation in his country. “If that’s how they grow cassava in his country [Greek], then I don’t know how they feed them,” Ababio said. The Debibi United CEO further urged the coach to concentrate on his professional responsibilities instead of making comments he considers inappropriate. “He should think about his job and stop saying nonsense. It was a reckless and unreasonable statement,” he added. Ababio’s response comes amid discussions surrounding the condition of the playing surface in Ghana football. Petros is one of the foreign coaches who have criticized the state of pitches in the country. Premier League debutants Debibi United top of the bottom three in the league after eight games with 7 points. On Sunday, Debibi United will face Hearts of Oak at the Debibi Presby Park. CEO Alexander Ababio said they are focused on remaining in the league. “Our target is to remain in the league despite our poor start to the season,” he said.

items.title: Niece and uncle shot dead at Sakumono over alleged GH¢500,000 debt
items.description: The police have launched investigations into the killing of a 57-year-old man and his 47-year-old niece at the NTHC Estate, Sakumono, in the Greater Accra Region, following a reported dispute over a GH¢500,000 debt. The deceased have been identified as George Atuguba and Irene Atuguba. A statement signed by Chief Superintendent Juliana Obeng, Head of Public Affairs at the Accra Regional Police Command on Friday, October 30, 2026, said officers were dispatched to the residence after the Sakumono District Police Command received information about the incident. The bodies of the two relatives were found lying in a pool of blood, the statement said. Debt dispute Preliminary police investigations suggest that the incident may have been triggered by a financial dispute involving George Atuguba, who had allegedly borrowed GH¢500,000 from a suspect but failed to repay the amount. The police identified the suspect as Samuel Christopher Osei Anto. According to the statement, the suspect reportedly went to the deceased’s residence on the morning of the incident with a woman identified as Beatrice Mumuni to demand repayment. A misunderstanding allegedly ensued, during which the suspect shot and killed George Atuguba and his niece, Irene Atuguba. The circumstances surrounding the reported shooting are still under investigation. Bodies sent for autopsy The police said the two victims were rushed to a hospital, where a medical officer pronounced them dead. Their bodies have since been deposited at the Police Hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy. The Accra Regional Police Command said efforts were being made to apprehend the suspect and bring him to justice.

items.title: Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win
items.description: Harry Kane won the Ballon d’Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday. The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition. Bayern Munich’s Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points. The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024. Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona. This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane. The Ballon d’Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings for men, and the top 50 for women. The post Organisers reveals how Kane edged Mbappe to Ballon d’Or win appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire : Ouattara met fin aux prorogations systématiques de retraite dans les institutions publiques
items.description: Dans une rupture nette avec les habitudes institutionnelles du pays, le président ivoirien Alassane Ouattara a tranché : les hauts fonctionnaires, officiers généraux et dirigeants d’entreprises publiques ayant dépassé l’âge légal de départ à la retraite ne bénéficieront plus de reconductions automatiques. Cette décision met un terme à la tradition des prorogations systématiques signées en fin d'année, frappant directement les sommets d’institutions clés comme le Conseil économique, social, environnemental et culturel (Cesec) ou l’Inspection générale d’État (IGE). En levant ce qui était perçu comme un verrou au renouvellement des compétences, la présidence ivoirienne impulse une rigueur accrue et prépare une redistribution majeure des postes stratégiques au sein de l'appareil étatique. C’est un tournant silencieux mais décisif qui s’opère dans les couloirs de la haute administration ivoirienne. Chaque fin d’année, le rituel était immuable : le chef de l’État apposait sa signature sur les décrets de prorogation, permettant à des figures influentes ayant atteint ou franchi la limite d’âge légale de demeurer à la tête de leurs structures. Cette pratique coutumière, solidement ancrée dans les mœurs de la haute fonction publique, appartient désormais au passé. Selon des informations concordantes, Alassane Ouattara a formellement décidé de ne plus reconduire ces dérogations d'âge, actant une rupture franche dans la gestion des carrières au sommet de l'État. La mesure ne souffre d’aucune exception sectorielle et touche les piliers de l’appareil d'État. Le coup d'arrêt concerne aussi bien les gestionnaires des sociétés d'État et des établissements publics que les commandants et officiers généraux des forces armées. Les présidences d’institutions constitutionnelles sont également en première ligne. Parmi les personnalités de premier plan directement visées par ce rappel à la règle figurent notamment les responsables du Conseil économique, social, environnemental et culturel (Cesec) ainsi que de l’Inspection générale d’État (IGE), deux organes névralgiques du dispositif de gouvernance et de contrôle ivoirien. Au-delà du simple respect de la réglementation, cette décision envoie un signal politique fort. Longtemps décriée par les observateurs et les cadres intermédiaires comme un obstacle majeur à la mobilité et à l’émergence de nouveaux profils dirigeants, la prolongation indéfinie des départs bloquait les perspectives d'évolution. En restaurant la rigueur réglementaire, le président ivoirien dessine les contours d'une respiration administrative attendue. Cet arbitrage ouvre grand la voie à d’importantes vagues de nominations et à une recomposition des états-majors dans plusieurs secteurs stratégiques de l’économie publique et de la gouvernance ivoirienne. L’article Côte d’Ivoire : Ouattara met fin aux prorogations systématiques de retraite dans les institutions publiques est apparu en premier sur NetAfrique.net .

items.title: Newsfile to discuss Mahama’s galamsey fight, GH¢49.72m evacuation controversy and five-year presidential term proposal
items.description: JoyNews’ flagship current affairs programme, Newsfile , will, this Saturday, October 31, discuss the progress of President John Mahama’s administration’s fight against illegal mining, renewed questions over the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating Ghanaians from South Africa, and the debate over extending Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years. The programme, hosted by Samson Lardy Anyenini, will bring these issues under scrutiny as questions continue to emerge over government policy, public accountability and the country’s constitutional arrangements. First, the programme will examine the government’s fight against illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, and whether the measures being implemented are delivering sustainable results. President John Mahama recently disclosed that more than 8,200 items used in illegal mining had been confiscated, including 135 excavators and almost 200 firearms. He has also announced plans to reclaim 5,000 acres of degraded land from 2027, with GH¢200 million allocated for the exercise. The government has also outlined plans to expand river protection operations and sustain enforcement in areas cleared of illegal miners. But with concerns about the continued impact of illegal mining on water bodies, forests and farmlands, the discussion will examine whether the interventions are translating into lasting progress and what more needs to be done to protect the country’s natural resources. Read more: Mahama says government has seized 8,200 items in galamsey fight . The second issue will focus on the GH¢49.72 million spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians from South Africa following renewed xenophobic attacks. The expenditure has come under scrutiny from the Minority, which has raised concerns about alleged discrepancies in flight records, payment registers and supporting documents. The caucus has called for an independent investigation into the exercise. The debate has also featured questions about the number of people evacuated and how the funds were disbursed, with government officials defending the expenditure and insisting that the records account for the money spent. Newsfile will examine the concerns raised by the opposition, the government’s explanations and whether the available records provide sufficient answers about the cost and management of the evacuation. Read more: Minority demands independent probe into South Africa evacuation costs . The third topic will consider former President John Agyekum Kufuor’s support for a proposal to extend Ghana’s presidential term from four to five years. Mr Kufuor has argued that the current four-year arrangement leaves governments with limited time to develop and implement policies before attention shifts to the next election. He maintains that a five-year term would give administrations more time to deliver on their programmes, while retaining the existing two-term limit. His position, however, differs from that of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), which has rejected the proposed extension and called for the retention of the four-year term. With the proposal forming part of the ongoing constitutional review process, the discussion will examine whether a longer presidential term would improve governance and policy implementation or weaken regular electoral accountability. Read more: Kufuor makes case for a five-year presidential term . The three issues raise important questions about the effectiveness of government interventions, accountability in the use of public resources and the constitutional arrangements that shape Ghana’s democracy. Newsfile airs live on Saturday, October 31, from 8:00 am to 12 noon on JoyNews, Joy 99.7 FM and Luv 99.5 FM, with Samson Lardy Anyenini as host.

items.title: Crypto giant Binance attempting to recover $6.3bn stolen in hack linked to North Korea
items.description: Binance’s co-CEO Richard Teng said: “This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.” Teng also describes how the hackers used “a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate”. Initially, the company had indicated the breach “may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop” but later statements have pointed to a broader breach. In a later update, the firm set it had “set aside” more than $6.34B in company funds to cover the stolen assets and was “actively buying” a range of crypto tokens. The Binance hack spooked cryptocurrency markets on Friday. The price of Bitcoin was down 5% to $76,800 in Friday afternoon trading in New York. Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase was down 12% as investors also reacted to earnings results in which the firm reported revenue slightly below expectations. Robinhood, a financial services company that trades in cryptocurrency, was down 7.8%. Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide. The company said in 2024 that it had more than $160bn in assets under its custody. A lot of the fear right now from Binance users – and the crypto industry at large – is whether or not Binance will actually be capable of covering this enormous financial loss. The company has said repeatedly that customer funds will be covered and that the firm is strong enough to weather the storm. But crypto history watchers have been pointing out online that this is exactly the kind of message that FTX CEO Sam Bankman-Fried gave before his crypto exchange collapsed in 2022, leading to huge losses for customers and the industry. Several experts have warned customers not to regard Binance’s promise to cover losses as legally binding and said they may need to pursue litigation to recover them. Daniel Tunkel, of the London-based Edwin Coe law firm, said that would “come down to what [customers] have been promised in their contracts”, and “where Binance can be sued for non-performance, if it comes to it”. Binance has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world. Meanwhile, AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said that several elements of the attack resembled earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack. In the last five years the crypto industry has been beset by enormous losses from hackers. In nearly all cases investigators have blamed hackers from North Korea, pointing to the infamous Lazarus Group – also know as TraderTraitor. The names refer to clusters of cyber criminals accused of working directly for the regime. Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, said it had “high confidence” that a North Korean is linked to the hack. North Korea is an impoverished country with very little industry and heavy international sanctions and experts say the regime uses cyber crime as a way to bring money in. North Korea has always denied this, but the wealth of evidence from cryptocurrency flow analysis and insider interviews from defectors is compelling. It makes North Korea likely to be the only nation that uses hacking as a way to raise public funds.

items.title: Amansie Community Bank posts GH₵73m profit before tax, unprecedented GH₵1bn deposit in Ashanti Region
items.description: Amansie Community Bank PLC is streamlining its operations to sustain gains after posting a strong financial performance in the year ended December 2025. The bank recorded more than 100 per cent increase in profit before tax, posting over 73 million cedis as against profits made in the preceding year. The bank also chalked up an unprecedented milestone as the first community bank in the Ashanti region to mobilize one billion cedis in deposits. The Amansie Community Bank increased its deposit mobilization by 48 per cent over the 2024 figure of 687.82 million cedis to a record of one billion cedis in 2025. The new record positions the financial institution as the first community bank to achieve this impressive feat in the Ashanti region. The deposits were made primarily into the Savings and Susu accounts of the bank, providing increased stability for utilization by the bank. A net amount of 80 million cedis was granted as loans and advances in the year 2025, representing 77 per cent over the previous year. The total assets also increased from 761.7 million cedis in 2024 to 1,156.7 billion cedis in 2025, representing 51.8 per cent. This gain was made possible through investments, cash and Bank Balances, and Loans and Advances. In 2024, the bank posted 36 million cedis in profit before tax, but it is now seeing 100 per cent increase (73 million cedis), attributable to improved income generated from credit and investment operations. The bank made a profit after tax of 50.98 million cedis as against the 2024 figure of 26.20 million cedis, representing an increase of 94.57 per cent. The bank’s portfolio investments increased by 35.2 per cent in the period under review to close at 739.3 million cedis from 546.7 million cedis in 2024. The investment funds were allocated to treasury bills, fixed deposits, and other short-term fixtures on the money market. A total dividend of 10.19 million cedis, representing 0.1459 cedis per dividend, has been recommended for payment to all shareholders with a total qualifying share of 69,877,568. The figure represents a 94 per cent increase in dividend per share over the 2024 dividend payout. Speaking at the bank’s 41st annual general meeting, the Chief Executive Officer of the bank, Frederick Kwakye Kyei, noted that prudent fiscal measures and operational efficiencies are required to sustain the gains of the bank in the ensuing years. “For the past three years, we’ve been very consistent after obtaining approval from the Bank of Ghana. All that is required is that we need to generate more revenue and get more profits. As we are increasing the number of shares, we are able to pay out more dividends,” he said. The bank remains committed to serving the financial needs of its customers and enhancing other banking platforms, including digital means. Board Chairman, Ben Kwakye-Adeefe, stressed that the management is focusing strategically on ways to generate funds from the micro-finance sector and providing credit facilities to medium, small and micro-scale businesses. He further noted that management is considering laying before shareholders a proposal to support struggling community banks to meet their minimum capital requirement. “We are also looking at how to mobilize funds from the micro-finance sector, especially where the Bank of Ghana is ensuring that the SMEs must be established and concentrated on and also help them access funding. We are also looking at how to help other community banks to be able to get the minimum capital requirement,” he said. Following the resumption of the Amansie Bank Scholarship Scheme in 2025, the bank invested 47,500 cedis in the educational successes of ten (10) students, covering the full tuition of beneficiaries.

items.title: Boxe : Sou Toké « Le Bombardier » livrera son dernier combat ce samedi au Palais des sports de Ouaga 2000
items.description: Le jubilé d'or de Sou Toké Patrice, qui mettra un terme à une riche carrière professionnelle, servira également de lancement officiel à « Faso Bolokourou », sa structure de promotion de la boxe burkinabè, ce samedi 31 octobre 2026 au Palais des sports de Ouaga 2000. Six combats sont programmés, dont l'ultime affrontement du champion burkinabè face au Béninois Anicet Amoussou. Le rideau tombera sur l'une des plus illustres carrières de la boxe burkinabè. Sou Toké Patrice, surnommé « Le Bombardier du Faso », dispute au Palais des sports de Ouaga 2000 son ultime combat professionnel à l'occasion d'un Gala jubilé d'or qui comprend six affrontements, dont deux combats professionnels et quatre amateurs. L'apothéose de la soirée opposera le champion burkinabè au Béninois Anicet Amoussou, dit « Le Poison ». L'ultime combat opposera Le Bombardier à Poison du Bénin Sou Toké a tenu à rassurer sur son état de forme et la qualité de sa préparation, quelques jours avant ce qui constitue l'aboutissement d'un parcours débuté il y a plus de deux décennies. Le comité d'organisation a pour sa part affirmé que toutes les dispositions sont prises pour offrir un Gala à la hauteur du palmarès de « Le Bombardier » et pour le lancement officiel de Faso Bolokourou, la structure de promotion que le boxeur entend porter après avoir raccroché les gants. Le comité d'organisation a appelé la population à venir massivement au Palais des sports pour saluer celui qui fut double champion d'Afrique, en 2007 et 2013, et détenteur de plusieurs ceintures continentales et internationales. Sou Toké Le Bombardier invitant les populations à sortir massivement La soirée ne se limitera pas à l'adieu sportif du champion. Quatre autres combats figurent à l'affiche. Janu Akadé, du Nigeria, va affronter le Burkinabè Ousmane Nikiema. Aziz Kinda, du Burkina Faso, sera opposé au Nigérian Kayile B. Raymond Sanou, autre Burkinabè, va en découdre avec le Nigérian Ola Padé. Autant de confrontations qui traduisent l'ambition du comité d'organisation de renouer avec l'intensité des grands galas d'antan. Rappelons que Faso Bolokourou dont le nom signifie « coup de poing au Faso » en dioula, se donne pour mission de relancer la boxe professionnelle burkinabè, de faire émerger une nouvelle génération de talents et de redonner à la discipline la ferveur qu'elle avait connue dans les années 2000. Le comité d'organisation prévoit notamment d'organiser régulièrement des combats amateurs et professionnels afin d'offrir aux jeunes boxeurs burkinabè des opportunités de se mesurer à la concurrence internationale. Minute.bf

items.title: Le Maroc satisfait de la non reconduction du mandat de la Minurso et demeure fermement attaché au respect de son intégrité territoriale
items.description: A l'issue de la séance de vote au Conseil de sécurité de l'ONU, le Maroc a exprimé sa satisfaction de la non reconduction du mandat de la Minurso qui tourne une page de 35 ans. Il a également assuré demeurer fermement attaché au strict respect du cessez-le-feu et de son intégrité territoriale, indique un communiqué du Cabinet Royal. En voici le texte : « Le mandat de la Minurso n’a pas été reconduit par le Conseil de sécurité des Nations Unies lors de sa réunion de ce jour, 30 octobre 2026. Il s’agit d’une évolution importante et d’un pas significatif vers la clôture définitive du dossier du Sahara marocain aux Nations Unies. Ce développement majeur coïncide avec la célébration de la fête de l’Unité, décrétée par Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L’assiste, pour incarner la rupture dans la gestion de ce dossier, passant d’une simple logique de gestion à une approche de transformation profonde des paramètres. Ainsi, la non-reconduction du mandat de la Minurso signifie clairement que la présence de cette Mission dans les provinces du sud du Royaume, notamment à travers son personnel, ses véhicules, son matériel et ses symboles, devrait cesser dans les prochains jours. C’est une page de 35 ans qui est désormais tournée. Héritée d’un contexte anachronique et révolu, cette Mission a longtemps constitué un instrument d’internationalisation du différend régional relatif au recouvrement légitime par le Royaume du Maroc de ses provinces sahariennes. En outre, la non-reconduction de la Minurso devrait marquer la fin de la saisine du Conseil de sécurité et le retrait de cette question de son ordre du jour. Dès lors, les réunions statutaires périodiques du Conseil consacrées au Sahara marocain, les rapports du Secrétaire général des Nations Unies y afférents et les briefings de son Envoyé personnel, n’auraient plus lieu d’être. Le processus politique onusien, qui a été marqué malheureusement par les tergiversations des autres parties, leur entêtement à créer le blocage et à faire perdurer le statu quo, se trouve ainsi suspendu. Des actions similaires seront également menées prochainement au sein des autres organes de l’ONU. Tout en marquant sa satisfaction de cette évolution, le Maroc demeure fermement attaché au cessez-le-feu, dans le strict respect de son intégrité territoriale, de sa sécurité nationale et de la quiétude de ses citoyens. Par ailleurs, la dynamique internationale lancée par Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu Le préserve, se poursuivra, aux niveaux bilatéral et régional. Elle a d’ores et déjà permis de capitaliser des soutiens importants, puisque plus des deux tiers des membres de l’ONU, y compris des membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité et les puissances influentes, appuient clairement l’autonomie, sous souveraineté marocaine, comme seul cadre de solution pour régler ce différend régional ». items.title: Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes
items.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, has reportedly escaped unhurt after suspected gunmen opened fire on his convoy near the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport on Friday night. The incident occurred at about 9pm on October 30, 2026, shortly after Dan’iya had escorted former Sokoto State Governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, to the airport. The candidate’s bulletproof sports utility vehicles were reportedly damaged in the shooting. Confirming the incident, the Sokoto State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Ahmad Rufae, said the command had received a report of the incident at the airport and would take necessary action. He added that anyone found culpable would be dealt with in accordance with the law. In a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, Dan’iya alleged that personnel of the Sokoto Marshal and the Sokoto State Community Guard blocked his convoy and prevented it from passing through the airport area. According to the statement, the personnel claimed they were acting on directives from their superiors not to allow ADC members into Sokoto State. It further alleged that attempts by members of Dan’iya’s security team to resolve the confrontation failed before gunshots were fired, damaging the candidate’s bulletproof vehicles. The statement also claimed that two Department of State Services (DSS) operatives attached to the candidate’s security team were detained during the confrontation. Dan’iya described the incident as a threat to his personal safety and a development capable of undermining democratic freedoms, political participation and peaceful coexistence in the state. The ADC candidate also alleged that earlier on Friday, his team had observed unusual deployments of Sokoto Marshal and Community Guard personnel at various entry points into the state, where vehicles bearing ADC inscriptions were allegedly stopped from entering. He said what initially appeared to be routine security operations had raised concerns about a possible attempt to restrict the movement and political activities of opposition members. “If security personnel can block a gubernatorial candidate, fire gunshots during a confrontation, damage his vehicle and detain officers assigned to his protection, then the people of Sokoto deserve urgent answers. “No one should be above the law, and no security outfit should be used to threaten political opponents,” Dan’iya was quoted as saying. The candidate disclosed that he had visited the Commissioner of Police in the state to formally report the incident, present his account of what transpired and seek intervention. He called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the DSS and other relevant security authorities to investigate the incident, identify those responsible and determine whether any unlawful orders had been issued. Dan’iya also demanded the immediate release of the two DSS operatives, if they remained in custody, and urged the authorities to preserve available video footage, operational records, eyewitness accounts and other evidence for an impartial investigation. He appealed to the Federal Government, the National Assembly, human rights organisations and the international community to pay attention to the security situation in Sokoto, warning that political intimidation and violence could threaten the credibility of the democratic process. The ADC candidate also challenged the Sokoto State Government to clarify the alleged directives attributed to the security personnel and ensure that state-controlled security outfits operated within the law and without political interference. “Sokoto is not the property of any government or political party. Every Nigerian has the right to enter the state, move freely and participate in lawful political activities. Any order intended to exclude ADC members from Sokoto would be unacceptable and must be investigated,” he said. Despite the incident, Dan’iya urged his supporters to remain calm, avoid provocation and refrain from retaliation, insisting that neither intimidation nor violence would make him or the ADC abandon their constitutional and democratic rights. He said he would continue to pursue his political ambition peacefully and lawfully, while urging security agencies to protect citizens irrespective of their political affiliations. The allegations contained in the ADC statement had yet to be independently verified as of the time of filing this report. There was also no official response from the Sokoto State Government, the Sokoto Marshal or the Community Guard explaining their account of the incident. The police and other relevant security authorities are expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding the reported shooting, the alleged detention of the DSS operatives and the damage to the candidate’s convoy. The post Gunmen attack ADC guber candidate’s convoy in Sokoto, candidate escapes appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PLF 2027 : vers un nouvel encadrement du télétravail et des emplois émergents
items.description: Le télétravail pourrait bientôt disposer d’un cadre juridique au Maroc. Le gouvernement d’El Mansouri prévoit d’engager, dès 2027, une réforme du Code du travail destinée à intégrer les nouvelles formes d’emploi, dont le travail à distance, le travail via les plateformes numériques et l’activité à temps partiel. Une évolution qui intervient alors que le recours au télétravail s’est développé depuis la pandémie de Covid-19, soulevant des questions sur la formalisation des relations contractuelles et la protection des droits des salariés. Cette orientation figure dans la note de présentation du projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027. Le document affiche une ambition plus large : faire de la qualité de l’emploi un axe central de la politique gouvernementale, en subordonnant les aides publiques au respect d’exigences minimales, au renforcement des contrôles et à la reconnaissance des entreprises qui offrent les meilleures conditions de travail. La révision du Code du travail doit notamment permettre d'adapter la législation à des modalités d’emploi qui se développent particulièrement parmi les jeunes. L'objectif affiché est de leur garantir une couverture sociale et des conditions de travail décentes, quelle que soit la forme d'activité exercée. Dans le prolongement de cette réforme, l'exécutif envisage l'adoption d'une « Charte du travail décent ». Les entreprises bénéficiant d'un soutien public à l’emploi seraient tenues de fournir à leurs salariés un contrat de travail déclaré et une couverture sociale dès le premier jour d'activité. Elles devraient également respecter les horaires légaux ainsi que les normes de santé et de sécurité au travail. La charte prévoit, en outre, leur participation à la recherche de solutions aux difficultés liées au transport ou au logement, lorsque les circonstances le nécessitent. Autre dispositif annoncé : la création d'un label « Employeur exemplaire », qui distinguerait les entreprises garantissant de bonnes conditions professionnelles. Les structures labellisées pourraient bénéficier d'un accès préférentiel aux marchés publics et aux mécanismes de soutien public. La qualité de l’emploi devrait également devenir un critère d'évaluation des programmes publics dédiés à l’emploi. Leur performance ne serait plus appréciée à travers le seul nombre de postes créés, mais aussi au regard de leur durabilité et des conditions dans lesquelles ils sont exercés. Des revalorisations salariales dans les secteurs public et privé La note de présentation dresse également le bilan des mesures engagées en matière d’emploi au titre de 2026. Elle met notamment en avant les revalorisations salariales dans la fonction publique, matérialisées par des augmentations directes des rémunérations, accompagnées d'une révision de l'impôt sur le revenu au profit de l'ensemble des fonctionnaires et agents de l'État et des établissements publics. Entre 2021 et 2026, le salaire minimum dans la fonction publique a ainsi progressé de 34 %, tandis que le salaire moyen a augmenté de 30 %. Dans le secteur privé, les revalorisations ont également concerné les deux principaux minima salariaux. Le salaire minimum interprofessionnel garanti (SMIG), applicable aux activités non agricoles, a enregistré une hausse de 21 % sur la même période. Le salaire minimum agricole garanti (SMAG) a, pour sa part, progressé de 27 %. La réforme fiscale en faveur des retraités figure également parmi les mesures mises en avant. Après une réduction de 50 % de l'impôt sur le revenu appliqué à leurs pensions à compter du 1er janvier 2025, ceux-ci bénéficient d'une exonération totale depuis le 1er janvier 2026. Sur le plan législatif, l'année 2026 a été marquée par l'adoption de la loi n° 032.26, complétant l'article 193 de la loi n° 65.99 portant Code du travail. Cette modification vise à réduire la durée quotidienne de travail des agents de gardiennage et de sécurité privée employés sous contrat par des entreprises spécialisées. Enfin, la lutte contre le travail des enfants a enregistré une évolution significative. En 2025, environ 103 000 enfants étaient concernés, représentant 1,3 % de la tranche d'âge visée. Ce nombre a diminué de 58,3 % par rapport à 2017. The post PLF 2027 : vers un nouvel encadrement du télétravail et des emplois émergents appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Two Unit Committee members among 4 arrested for leasing land to galamsey operators after Abesua bridge collapse
items.description: Two Unit Committee members are among four persons arrested in connection with illegal mining activities that led to the collapse of the bridge over River Kukubu in the Abesua community of the Atwima Mponua District in the Ashanti Region. The other two suspects are illegal miners who were operating along the riverbanks. The bridge, which is the only access route linking Abesua No.1, Abesua No.2, Nyamebekyere, Abrokyire and adjoining communities to the main road at Serebuoso and Mankranso, caved in after galamsey operators excavated and degraded lands around it, causing the river to overflow onto the road and cutting off the communities. The arrests follow public outcry and an exclusive report filed by JoyNews, which showed the extent of devastation caused by the illegal mining activities. Confirming the arrests, the District Chief Executive for Atwima Mponua, Ibrahim Issahak, disclosed that preliminary investigations have established a direct link between some local leaders and the illegal miners. According to Mr. Issahak, the two unit committee members allegedly collected money from the miners and leased out parcels of land around the bridge and along the river buffer zone for illegal mining. “The illegal miners themselves accused the unit committee members of taking money from them and leasing to them. That is what our initial investigations point to,” the DCE stated. He said the four suspects are currently in police custody, assisting with investigations, and will be arraigned before court by Monday, November 3, 2026, to face charges relating to illegal mining and causing damage to public infrastructure. The collapse of the bridge has had dire consequences for the affected communities. Residents say economic activities have come to a standstill as farmers are unable to transport their produce to market centres at nearby urban communities. Health delivery has also been affected, with patients struggling to access the nearest health facilities. The situation is most dire for schoolchildren. Pupils from the cut-off communities who commute daily to Atwima Asamang Basic School often have to abandon school, especially during rainfall, as they are unable to cross the swollen river. In response, the DCE, together with the District Engineer and a technical team from the Assembly, has visited the site to assess the damage and commence emergency repair works. Mr. Issahak disclosed that, as an interim measure, runoff water has been drained from the affected stretch, the clogged bridge culvert has been cleared, and reinforcement works using boulders, chippings and gravel are ongoing to make the road motorable while plans for a permanent reconstruction are considered. He assured residents that the Assembly is committed to fully restoring the road and will ensure that all persons found culpable in the illegal mining activities that led to its destruction face the full rigours of the law. “We will not shield anyone. If you are found to have leased land for galamsey around this critical bridge, you will face the law. We must protect public infrastructure,” he warned. Mr. Issahak also cautioned other unit committee members and opinion leaders in the district against engaging in similar acts, stressing that the Assembly will not hesitate to prosecute anyone who facilitates illegal mining in water bodies and along road reserves. Meanwhile, residents of the communities affected by the collapse of the bridge have applauded the government, through the District Assembly, for its swift intervention to restore access. According to them, the emergency works have brought huge relief, as they can now access the main road at Serebuoso and Mankranso to go about their daily activities. Farmers are able to transport their produce to market centres, while schoolchildren can now go to school and return home safely without having to cross the dangerous, flooded river. They, however, say the current intervention is only a temporary measure and are urging the District Assembly to take concrete steps to fulfil its promise of constructing a new, permanent bridge over River Kukubu to prevent future occurrences and ensure the long-term safety of commuters.

items.title: Législatives en Israël: Isaac Herzog, un président au cœur des tractations
items.description: Les élections législatives en Israël se sont achevées sans majorité claire. Benyamin Netanyahu et son rival Gadi Eisenkot vont devoir élargir leur bloc pour espérer former un gouvernement. Il reviendra finalement au président israélien, Isaac Herzog, de désigner celui qui sera chargé de constituer une coalition. Une responsabilité majeure pour ce président dont la fonction est pourtant essentiellement honorifique. Son choix reste difficile à anticiper.

items.title: Plusieurs cadres nommés au ministère de l’Assainissement (décret)

items.title: NDLEA: No payment for drug tests by Interior Ministry recruits
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has announced that applicants undergoing recruitment into four agencies under the Ministry of Interior will not be required to pay for the mandatory Drug Integrity Test (DIT). The agencies are the Nigerian Correctional Service, Nigeria Immigration Service, Federal Fire Service and Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. The NDLEA said arrangements had been concluded for the exercise, adding that the Ministry of Interior had made bulk payment to cover the testing of all new recruits. Consequently, candidates and personnel participating in the exercise were advised not to make any payment to NDLEA officials, testing centres or through any other payment channel. The agency’s spokesman, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement, explaining that candidates would be required to access the NDLEA Drug Integrity Test portal through a designated link or access point to be provided on their respective institutional portals. He said the arrangement was designed to ensure a seamless and orderly testing process. According to Babafemi, the portal would enable candidates to complete the necessary registration and documentation before proceeding with the test without making additional payments. The statement added that the agency appreciated the cooperation of the Ministry of Interior and remained committed to ensuring a smooth, transparent and efficient implementation of the exercise. items.title: CRIEF : 78 milliards de GNF en jeu, la défense de Mandian Sidibé conteste le rapport de l’IGE
items.description: Au terme d’une journée d’interrogatoire devant la Chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026, les avocats de Mandjan Sidibé et ceux de la partie civile ont livré des appréciations divergentes sur les débats. Alors que la défense estime que son client a apporté des éléments de réponse aux faits qui lui sont reprochés, la partie civile considère que plusieurs questions relatives à la gestion financière de l’Office guinéen de publicité (OGP) restent à éclaircir. Poursuivi pour des faits présumés de détournement portant sur 78 milliards de francs guinéens, l’ancien directeur général de l’OGP a notamment été interrogé sur sa gestion de la société et sur les conclusions du rapport de l’Inspection générale d’État (IGE), qu’il conteste. À la sortie de l’audience, son avocat, Me Seydou Traoré, s’est déclaré satisfait du déroulement des débats. Il estime que cette comparution a permis à son client de présenter sa version des faits devant la juridiction. « Aujourd’hui, nous avons eu l’occasion de nous exprimer librement sur un débat qui a fait tant de bruit dans la cité. Nous avons donné notre part de vérité. Au vu des débats, vous comprendrez que tout ce qui a été dit contre nous n’est pas fondé », a-t-il déclaré. La défense a particulièrement insisté sur les conditions d’élaboration du rapport de l’IGE. Me Seydou Traoré estime que son client n'a pas été associé à la procédure de vérification pour présenter ses observations. « Leur rapport doit être contradictoire. Or, Monsieur Mandjan n’a jamais été appelé pour donner sa version des faits », a-t-il soutenu. L'avocat a également rappelé que l'OGP est une société anonyme régie par les textes de l'OHADA. Il a évoqué la certification des comptes de l'exercice 2022-2023 par un commissaire aux comptes, affirmant que les états financiers concernés avaient été transmis à la Cour des comptes sans qu'aucune irrégularité ne soit relevée, selon les éléments qu'il a présentés. De son côté, Me Christophe Labilé Kolié, avocat de la partie civile, a mis l'accent sur les questions financières soulevées dans le dossier. Il estime que les explications de l'ancien directeur général doivent permettre de mieux comprendre les mouvements de fonds enregistrés pendant sa gestion. Il a notamment évoqué les variations de la masse salariale, les marchés publics et les différentes dépenses effectuées au sein de l'OGP. « Quand on gère, il faut pouvoir rendre compte et, lorsqu'il y a une procédure à suivre, il faut pouvoir la respecter », a déclaré l'avocat. Me Christophe Labilé Kolié a également soulevé la question de l'utilisation des ressources de la société et des versements éventuellement effectués au profit de l'État guinéen, présenté comme son unique actionnaire. Selon les chiffres que l'avocat de la partie civile a avancés à l'audience, sur un montant de 108 milliards de francs guinéens évoqué dans le dossier, 52 milliards auraient été consacrés à la masse salariale. Il estime que des précisions supplémentaires sont nécessaires sur les recettes, les dépenses et les paiements effectués durant la période concernée. Au-delà de ces positions divergentes, les débats ont principalement porté sur la portée du rapport de l'Inspection générale d'État, la gestion financière de l'OGP et les justifications attendues sur les opérations concernées. La Chambre de jugement de la CRIEF a finalement renvoyé l'affaire au 2 décembre 2026 pour la poursuite des débats.
